question: Can host roles and strictly earlier activity distinguish lateral movement from exfiltration?
limitations: Header-width mismatches are quarantined; their labels and features cannot be assigned without guessing the missing schema. All reported tactic counts are observed valid-width counts only.
Missing tactic means no matched source mapping, not a verified benign label. No explicit benign tactic value was found in qualified-width records.
The source rule layer maps literal commands and file paths to tactics. It does not prove successful lateral access or successful receipt of exfiltrated data.
The only valid-width run containing both target tags is APT28/Campaign 1, with three lateral and three exfiltration tagged records; those are correlated records, not six attacks.
APT10/Campaign 2 and APT32/Campaign 2 have byte-identical CSV content. They cannot be independent partitions.
APT41/Campaign 1 and APT29/Campaign 1 lateral tags include key-script/file activity on a single observed host, so they are not validated cross-host movement events.
APT3/Campaign 2 exfiltration-tagged messages contain missing-archive errors; APT32/Campaign 2 and its duplicate contain HTTP 501 unsupported POST errors.
The exported @timestamp lacks an explicit timezone and differs in semantics from embedded audit epoch; timestamps need normalization and event-availability qualification before causal history.

Campaign sequence JSONs describe intended Node/Tactic/Technique order, not timestamped success manifests. Host/container names and attack-box roles cannot establish generalizable host roles by themselves.
next_action: Do not fit the intended principal benign/lateral/exfiltration history benchmark on this release. Keep the pinned artifacts as a reproducible label-quality case; pursue a dataset with qualified both-stage executions and benign background, or obtain source schema and execution/success manifests before reconsideration.
